headline: Low pairwise risk overall: no shared channels or write surfaces are documented, so injection, leakage, and conflict pathways are not evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel, filesystem bridge, or parser path is documented for botpress and langchain4j. Both profiles show empty io_surfaces and no evidence of one ingesting the other's outputs by default, so a prompt-injection pathway is not supported.
conditions: IF a shared clipboard, filesystem, or MCP bridge is added between botpress and langchain4j, reassess injection risk.
IF either agent begins parsing the other's raw text as instructions, the pathway becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared workspace.
Disable any future copy-paste or message-queue bridge between them.
Add provenance tags before any cross-agent handoff.
requires-engineering: enforce content-type separation for tool outputs versus instructions.

B_data_leakage.rationale: The profiles do not show shared storage, shared OAuth, or any data classes touched by either botpress or langchain4j. With network egress set to none on both and empty data_classes_touched, there is no documented leakage path between them.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted access to the same workspace or credentials, leakage risk must be re-evaluated.
IF either agent is configured to upload file contents to a backend, cross-agent exposure becomes possible.
mitigations: Do not mount a shared filesystem.
Keep credentials separate per agent.
Review any future upload or logging settings.
requires-engineering: add per-agent data-loss-prevention controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write surface is documented. botpress only shows install_packages and no write or network egress, while langchain4j shows only network_egress:none; neither profile exposes filesystem, git, or database writes, so a direct capability conflict is not evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents are later given write access to the same directory or mutable resource, conflict risk becomes plausible.
IF an orchestrator adds shared locking-free state, reassess for race conditions.
mitigations: Avoid granting shared write permissions.
Run each agent in its own working directory.
Keep mutable state externalized behind a single writer.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: There is no evidence that langchain4j treats botpress output as authoritative or that botpress produces downstream facts for langchain4j to act on. With both profiles lacking documented action-taking authority and no evidence bundle, a cascading-error chain is not supported.
conditions: IF botpress outputs are wired directly into langchain4j prompts without verification, the risk becomes real.
IF langchain4j is configured to execute actions from botpress text, reassess immediately.
mitigations: Insert a human or rule-based verification step.
Require structured schemas for any handoff.
Log and review cross-agent prompts before execution.
requires-engineering: add validation gates for factual claims.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either botpress or langchain4j. Because the profiles are silent on compliance-relevant data flows, there is no specific mismatch to cite; the other agent is not cited beyond confirming the absence of such fields.
conditions: IF regulated data classes such as PHI or EU PII are introduced into either agent, compliance must be reassessed.
IF retention or residency policies differ after deployment, the verdict changes.
mitigations: Classify data before routing it to either agent.
Keep regulated data out of both agents until policies are defined.
Document retention and residency settings.
requires-engineering: implement policy enforcement for regulated data.
